findings.title: Preserve UTF-8 across the new Windows PowerShell 5.1 agent boundary
findings.description: The editor explicitly launches WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell.exe with -NoProfile. The new launcher pipes $prompt to native Codex without setting $OutputEncoding (Windows PowerShell 5.1 defaults to ASCII), so a non-ASCII workspace or candidate path is sent as question marks. Independently, plan.json and deployment.json are written as BOMless UTF-8 but read by Get-Content -Raw without -Encoding UTF8, which uses the legacy ANSI default in Windows PowerShell 5.1. The returned path therefore fails the exact inventory allowlist at lines218-221 or reaches GitHub/native activation with a corrupted path. This blocks automatic setup for common Chinese/non-ASCII user or workspace locations despite the candidate being executable and valid.
findings.requested_change: Use an explicit UTF-8 native-stdin boundary (save/restore $OutputEncoding appropriately, or an equivalent controlled process input stream) and explicit UTF-8 decoding of both JSON reads; add a fixture with actual non-ASCII workspace/runtime paths and a native child that checks received stdin bytes. Preserve the existing allowlist and do not normalize away corruption.
findings.validation_basis: Static code/PowerShell 5.1 encoding semantics; no PowerShell runtime available here. Existing added fixture paths and summaries are ASCII. The known #91 seam changes configure_gonggong_runtime.ps1 and two requirements fixtures, not this newly added launcher; integrating that seam alone will not repair these boundaries.
